purpose: Track whether InfRing preserves the useful native features of external agent frameworks when they run through the Gateway Agent Runtime socket.
non_authority: This contract does not make a runtime reliable.
This contract does not prove native InfRing intelligence.
This contract does not authorize Shell, adapters, or external engines to bypass Gateway.
This contract does not turn private runtime slash or CLI commands into raw passthrough chat prompts.

promotion_scope.rule: Codex and Claude Code are the golden external runtime pair. Other runtimes may be cataloged or selectable, but they must not be promoted until they pass this same feature-parity matrix with compact evidence.

feature_dimensions.title: Context continuity
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Can the runtime see enough prior InfRing conversation context to continue naturally without starting cold?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway projects bounded context packs from canonical InfRing context authority.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Shell-owned prompt stuffing or engine-private memory replacing InfRing context.

feature_dimensions.title: Transcript persistence
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Are user messages, assistant responses, terminal failures, and compact work summaries persisted as canonical conversation records?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway writes transcript projections and compact refs; Shell only renders them.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Visual-only external runtime messages that disappear on reload.

feature_dimensions.title: Activity and decision trace
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Does InfRing preserve useful runtime activity and decision/dialog text in a concise collapsible turn summary?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Adapters translate private stream events; Gateway normalizes bounded activity projections.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Raw process dumps, generic Started/Done rows, or Shell-authored interpretation.

feature_dimensions.title: Slash and CLI command catalog
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Are native runtime slash/CLI controls visible as canonical InfRing command intents with operational status?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway command catalog projects runtime commands and InfRing native commands.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Shell executing raw runtime commands or hiding unwired commands as if they work.

feature_dimensions.title: Runtime command execution
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Can safe runtime commands execute or return an honest manual-action/projection-only state through Gateway?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway admits command intents and adapters translate private runtime syntax.

feature_dimensions.title: Runtime model projection
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Does the active runtime expose truthful model rows without fake defaults, stale rows, or wrong provider menus?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway projects available models and capability states; Shell renders rows.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Dashboard-owned model truth or cross-runtime stale menu leakage.

feature_dimensions.title: Permission pause and resume
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Do risky actions pause before final answer, ask for approval, then resume or deny with receipts?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway owns pending request, resume token, decision admission, and receipt.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: External runtime converting blocked writes into final text without an approval opportunity.

feature_dimensions.title: Active turn steering contract
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Can a user steer an active external-runtime turn through Gateway without creating duplicate user bubbles, losing the steering text, or giving Shell runtime authority?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway owns steering admission and resume/follow-up semantics; Shell only renders the user steer row and submits the steering projection.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Shell treating active-turn steering as a normal chat send or reconstructing runtime steering behavior locally.

feature_dimensions.title: Artifact proposal and apply
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Can approved artifact proposals become real files through Gateway with verification evidence?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Durable effects require Gateway/Kernel-approved application and receipts.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: External engine direct write by default or Shell applying proposal payloads.

feature_dimensions.title: Working directory control
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Does the runtime honor the InfRing-selected working directory while preserving explicit out-of-tree permission boundaries?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway projects workspace scope and adapter launch context.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Hard-coded user paths or Shell-owned filesystem authority.

feature_dimensions.title: Hard failure projection
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Do usage limits, auth failures, provider outages, missing CLIs, and timeouts become visible chat terminal states with next actions?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Adapters classify provider/runtime failures; Gateway projects terminal outcome.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Silent drops, generic 502s, or raw stack traces as user-facing messages.

feature_dimensions.title: Stop and cancellation semantics
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Can a user stop a runtime turn and still receive a persisted visible stopped/interrupted transcript outcome?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway owns cancel intent projection and transcript terminal state.

feature_dimensions.title: Attachment and pasted-context bridge
feature_dimensions.parity_question: Can large pasted text and attachments become bounded refs the runtime can read without bloating chat context?
feature_dimensions.infRing_boundary: Gateway/context authority materializes refs; adapters receive bounded references.
feature_dimensions.forbidden_shortcut: Shell stuffing huge pasted text into chat memory.
